root_cause.text: The `scs_check_usage()` function passed an incorrect parameter type to `__scs_magic()`, passing a `struct task_struct *` pointer instead of a `void *` pointer to the shadow call stack memory, causing the function to calculate the wrong end address boundary for stack usage scanning.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 138 from `for (p = task_scs(tsk); p < __scs_magic(tsk); ++p)` to `for (p = task_scs(tsk); p < __scs_magic(task_scs(tsk)); ++p)`. The commit message explicitly states that `__scs_magic()` requires a `void *` parameter pointing to the shadow call stack (returned by `task_scs(tsk)`), but the buggy code was passing `tsk` (a `struct task_struct *`) instead. This caused the loop to scan an incorrect memory range, potentially leading to inaccurate stack usage reporting or kernel crashes when accessing unmapped memory.
